# Intake, exhaust and tuning

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Install a K&N FIPK Cold Air Induction system and connect it for improved throttle response. [t1090]

[Partial] Install a UHMWPE intake spacer on the NA motor and modify it for an SC setup. [t1326]

Install long tube headers to replace stock manifolds. [t2035]

[Partial] Install long tube headers with CEL eliminators, then ensure new manifold and crush gaskets fit. [t1738]

[Partial] Purchase and install a Supercharger radiator to replace the stock unit. [t1109]

[Partial] Remove the existing muffler and weld a straight pipe for the single outlet. [t1917]

[Partial] Install headers with flanges for an exhaust crossover, then have a shop cut them off and weld on new pipes. [t1917]

[Partial] Route the pipe as short as possible and ensure the exit dumps gases efficiently. [t1917]

Install an exhaust cutout valve to bypass the muffler while retaining it in place. [t1917]

[Partial] Remove the front driveshaft and replace sharp 90-degree bends in the exhaust piping. [t1917]

Install high-flow cats to maintain emissions legality while improving flow. [t1917]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Install long tube headers to replace the stock manifolds.
2. [Partial] Bolt in a test pipe or aftermarket cat-back exhaust section to bypass the secondary catalytic converters.

_Procedure reported by [t2035]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1738] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install long tube headers with CEL eliminators to bypass rear O2 sensor monitoring.
2. Ensure new manifold gaskets and crush gaskets are in place between the header and secondary catalytic converter.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1109] [Partial]</summary>

1. Purchase a Supercharger (SC) radiator from an aftermarket vendor.
2. [Partial] Install the new SC radiator to replace the stock unit.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1917] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the existing muffler or cut it out after a crossover section.
2. [Partial] Weld or clamp a straight piece of pipe to serve as the single outlet.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1917] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install headers with flanges designed to bolt up to an exhaust crossover.
2. [Partial] Have a shop cut off the header flange and weld new pipes directly, or use pre-bent pipe.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1917] [Partial]</summary>

1. Route the pipe as short as possible with few bends to maximize gas velocity.
2. [Partial] Ensure the exit dumps gases efficiently, potentially using a simple turn-down near the bumper.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1917] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the front driveshaft to gain clearance for working on the manifold.
2. [Partial] Replace sharp 90-degree bends in the exhaust piping with straighter sections or same-size tubing.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1326] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install a UHMWPE intake spacer on the NA motor if using an SC setup.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1917] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install an exhaust cutout valve to bypass the muffler while retaining it in place.

</details>

## Specifications

- **Crossover pipe diameter**: 2" [t1917] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Single outlet pipe diameter**: 2.5" [t1917] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Note the significant improvement in throttle response immediately after installation. [t1090]
- Modify the spacer slightly to fit the SC pattern. [t1326]
- Consider a body lift or cutting a hole in the hood if clearance is tight. [t1326]
- Use a 90-degree angled O2 sensor eliminator if space is tight between the body and exhaust. [t2035]
- If using an angled eliminator, ensure it fits without rubbing against surrounding panels. [t2035]
